evals.prompt: can you write a README for this repo? it's a little node CLI I made called `tidyjson` that sorts keys and normalises whitespace in JSON files. package.json has a bin entry, there's a test folder, no docs site.
evals.expected_output: Reads package.json, the bin entry, tests and source; runs `tidyjson --help` (or copies usage from tests) to capture real output. Recommends code-first (small CLI, value shows in a few commands, no docs site), using the decision table. Confirms with ONE AskUserQuestion call: the recommended option first with '(Recommended)', 2-3 options, each preview showing the first ~12 lines of tidyjson's own README in that style, and a second question for the trade-off or non-goal if the repo doesn't reveal one. Waits for the answer, records `style` in .claude/readme-authoring.json, drafts. The README opens with a specific claim, then install and a real before/after example; states a cost (e.g. what it doesn't handle). No emoji headings, no filler, no invented benchmarks. Runs readme_lint.py (score under 15) and readme_freshness.py check --full (no errors). Offers commit-time freshness checks in one line.
expectations: Asks exactly one AskUserQuestion call with the recommended style first and labelled (Recommended)
Previews use the real project name and real commands, not a generic template
Does not draft before the user answers
Every command in the final README was run or copied from tests/CI
Lint score under 15; freshness --full reports no errors

evals.prompt: Build me a small Python library that parses ISO-8601 durations (like P3DT4H) into timedelta objects, with tests, packaging via pyproject, and a README. Don't stop to ask me things, just get it done and tell me when it's finished.
evals.expected_output: Treats the README as one deliverable inside a long autonomous task, so it does NOT call AskUserQuestion for style. Picks code-first from the decision table (small library, value shows in a few lines), drafts using real output captured by running the example against the code just written, records the style in .claude/readme-authoring.json, runs the lint and freshness checks, and ends with a one-line report: style used, why, and how to switch. States a real limitation (e.g. no support for year/month components, because timedelta can't represent them) instead of claiming completeness.
expectations: No AskUserQuestion call for the README style
Final report names the chosen style, the reason, and how to switch
README example output matches what the code actually produces
README states at least one real limitation

evals.prompt:
[Hook context] README freshness (README.md): 3 finding(s)
  [error] removed-flag L41: README documents --legacy-format, which this change removes from the code.
  [warn] undocumented-flag: New flag --format is not mentioned in the README.
  [warn] surface-touched: Public-surface files changed (src/cli.ts, package.json) but README.md is not in this commit.

Run the readme-authoring skill in freshness mode on README.md (recorded style: code-first). Fix real staleness in the README; leave false positives alone. The commit is proceeding (warn mode); follow up with a README commit if the review finds real staleness.
evals.expected_output: Enters freshness mode. Runs readme_freshness.py check --json, reads the diff for src/cli.ts and package.json, confirms --legacy-format was replaced by --format, updates only the README lines that mention the old flag (keeping code-first style), adds --format where flags are documented, and judges the package.json change (e.g. a dependency bump) as not README-relevant. Lints the result, commits the README as a follow-up commit, and reports in one or two lines. Does not rewrite unrelated sections or use README_FRESHNESS_SKIP.
expectations: Edits only README lines affected by the diff
Classifies each finding (stale / false positive / needs user)
Makes a follow-up README commit because mode is warn
Does not use README_FRESHNESS_SKIP=1

evals.prompt: this README reads like chatgpt wrote it (it did lol). can you make it not suck? keep all the actual info
evals.expected_output: Uses the rewrite recipe. Runs readme_lint.py first and keeps the findings. Extracts every real fact (commands, flags, config keys, requirements, links) and verifies each against the code; drops or fixes those that don't verify and says which. Infers the existing project type, recommends a style and confirms it with one AskUserQuestion call (recommended first), unless a style is already recorded. Rebuilds around a specific claim, the smallest real example and a stated cost; removes emoji headings, filler, template sections, the directory tree and boilerplate contributing text. Re-lints and reports before/after scores and any facts it could not verify.
expectations: Reports lint score before and after
Every surviving fact was verified against the code
Lists facts that were dropped because they did not verify
No emoji headings, filler words or empty sections in the result

evals.prompt: can you make it so the README gets checked whenever you commit in this repo? warn me, don't block
evals.expected_output: Explains in one line what the check does, confirms target only if ambiguous (defaults to Claude's commits; offers the git pre-commit hook for the user's own commits), runs `readme_freshness.py enable --mode warn --target claude`, then `status`, and reports what was written: .claude/readme-authoring.json (enabled, warn), the PreToolUse hook in .claude/settings.local.json, and the .gitignore line. Mentions that the hook is live after Claude Code reloads settings (/hooks once, or restart). Does not enable block mode or touch an existing pre-commit hook.
expectations: Runs enable with --mode warn
Reports every file written or changed
Mentions the settings reload caveat
